key_insight: An exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion model shows that CT-CS energy alignment is the dominant lever controlling the trade-off between charge generation and voltage loss in organic photovoltaics, with triplet recycling kinetics modulating whether that balance is preserved.
engineering_relevance: The model gives device engineers actionable design rules for tuning singlet/triplet energetics and transfer rates to improve photocurrent while limiting voltage penalties in organic solar cells.
method: Couples exciton kinetics with drift-diffusion transport in a self-consistent device model
Solves singlet/triplet populations and reversible photophysical transitions for transient and steady-state response
Analyzes how LE-CT, CT-CS, and LE-T offsets plus triplet-transfer kinetics affect generation, recombination, extraction, and voltage loss
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model reproduces triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends.
watch_item: The predicted performance balance is highly sensitive to CT-CS alignment and small triplet-transfer offsets, so parameter accuracy is critical for reliable device design.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
